behaviorReferences.SUP-01: One independent native host/OMP pair per assignment, visible through its dedicated tmux pane. Driven per-run FIFO registration and keyed in-flight launch coalescing preserve ownership after waiter cancellation.
behaviorReferences.SUP-02: Host observation has bounded authenticated loopback requests and passive sequential journals. A timeout with exact live OS identities becomes degraded observation, without replacement or an automatic-cycle debit.
behaviorReferences.LIF-02: Stop fences launch admission, cancels observations, drains queued launches and stops the exact host, OMP and contained commands before claiming stopped ownership. Unclaimed queued attempts remain admitted.
behaviorReferences.LIF-04: Actual controller SIGKILL before dispatch, before PID persistence and after running identity uses durable descriptors to seal delayed helpers, stop old ownership or reattach the same processes and session. Actual Docker descendants are receipted and removed after host/controller death.
behaviorReferences.SEC-02: Private canonical roots and fixed origins, exact saved PIDs/session/backend and OS ownership constrain adoption and signaling. Wrong identities, engine outage and unreadable journals retain explicit holds.

auditCorrections: A new checked-owned helper mode execs the host in place, preserving the durable PID and terminal output. The existing captured checked Git mode is unchanged and rerun.
Launch descriptor/spec and private configuration precede tmux dispatch. Final store/control and controller authority validation enclose actual spawn; delayed dispatch after restart is sealed.
Launch, observation and cleanup workers are independently registered. Dropping an RPC waiter does not drop the admitted work. Close fences launch first, then drains all known and saved runs.
Complete malformed journal lines block recovery but cannot skip physical cleanup. Journal uncertainty and actual stopped ownership remain separate facts.
SQL read/receipt failure does not skip cleanup of other known hosts. Mismatched saved PIDs are never signaled; verified exact owned children can still be stopped while the mismatch stays held.
Host ownership is rechecked after stopping OMP because a descendant can retain the parent lease descriptor. Container final receipts precede removal; engine outage preserves uncertainty.
Replaced or dangling tool-directory links retain uncertain ownership even when their target appears empty; verified host/runner cleanup still completes.
Queued attempts that never claimed or launched remain admitted and are removed from the cancelled in-memory slot map, preventing false execution history or an unnecessary recovery cycle.
limitations: N3.3b1 accepts process supervision as a library. Workflow tool authorization, launch composition, delivery/transition/recovery decisions and scheduler/service integration remain N3.3b2/b3. Native daemon admission stays fenced.

OMP 18.4.12 runs under the existing OS offline guard with synthetic provider responses and credentials. The supervised send_message backend is a loopback fixture, not actual Mail. Full composed OMP/tmux/Mail/Docker workflow proof remains required.

The 17 new lifecycle cases use real native hosts, tmux, SQLite, process ownership and two actual Docker cleanup scenarios. Their runner replies and seeded workflow records are explicitly fixtures; four separate cases use actual OMP.
Legacy TypeScript ownership roots and schema/history/absolute-path restore remain N7. Missing native descriptors retain an ownership hold rather than becoming stopped proof.
N6 operator/terminal/accessibility and N7 installation/footprint/release cutover remain outstanding. The retained live pilot and real credentials were not used.
